evidence_excerpts: Almost immediately following his accident, R.B. was able to intentionally recall specific events temporally and spatially situated in his personal past, but his recollection of those events was compromised in an unusual manner — memory for those events, though fitting the standard criteria for episodic recollection, was not accompanied by a sense of personal ownership.

I was remembering scenes, not facts … I could clearly recall a scene of me at the beach in New London with my family as a child. But the feeling was that the scene was not my memory. As if I was looking at a photo of someone else’s vacation.
text: Episodic recollection can preserve temporally and spatially situated autobiographical content while lacking a felt sense of personal ownership.
